prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the nearby foreground path and shrubs from the more distant canyon walls and vehicles: brighter lower regions are nearer, while the dark ridge line is far away, although exact metric distance is not encoded. Across the five frames, the visible people appear roughly 3–7 m from the camera wearer, while the white vehicles are approximately 10–25 m away; the nearest person is left of the wearer in frame 1, moves into the front-left/centre in frame 2, is farther ahead in frame 3, and another person or group appears front-left in frame 5. The people remain much closer to the wearer than the vehicles and canyon walls, but nothing clearly falls within the wearer's arm's reach, and the shrubs may partly occlude the ground and distant objects. The map makes foreground-versus-background layering clearer than RGB, but it is unreliable around the bright sky, black image borders, object boundaries, and fine or distant structures, so metre estimates and person-to-person distances remain approximate.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates three person instances—in frames 1, 2, and 5—and a small truck-like instance in frame 4, placing the people at the extreme left edge, lower centre-left, and lower left-of-centre of their respective frames. In RGB context, the first person is partly cut off by the left image boundary at roughly 4–6 m, the second is about 3–5 m away and in front-left of the wearer, the frame-4 vehicle is roughly 10–20 m ahead, and the frame-5 person or group is about 4–7 m away with the more distant white vehicle behind and to the right. The masks clarify which visible pixels belong to detected people and the vehicle, including partial out-of-view extent, but they provide no depth, facing direction, gaze, above/below relation, or arm-reach information without the RGB and depth context. The map is unreliable because it misses most vehicles, terrain, vegetation, and possibly additional people or body parts, and the tiny frame-4 truck label may not match the visible vehicle precisely.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black in all five frames, so it supplies no detected body or hand skeletons and therefore no direct evidence about limb locations, facing direction, gaze, interpersonal orientation, or reach. Using RGB alone, the frame-1 person is partly out of view at the far left and appears roughly 4–6 m away, the frame-2 person is approximately 3–5 m ahead-left and oriented mostly sideways, and the later person or group is roughly 4–7 m ahead-left; none is clearly within the camera wearer's arm's reach. Across the strip, people shift from the left edge to a more central foreground position and later reappear farther right in the scene, while vehicles remain farther ahead, but the blank pose output cannot establish approach, retreat, or turning reliably. Its failure to mark even clearly visible people makes it unreliable for every requested skeletal or hand-based spatial relation.
